explanation: The sentence describes what had happened before Zhao's win: only one other woman had ever won best director. 'Previously' signals that earlier time. 'As a result' is wrong because Bigelow's earlier win was not caused by Zhao's win.

The previous sentence says the turbines are off the Virginia coast; this sentence gives the precise details (176 turbines, 27 miles east of Virginia Beach). 'To be exact' introduces that more precise version. 'As a result' fails because the turbine count is not a consequence of the location.

Dowsett wanted to coordinate suffragists' efforts, and founding the association was an action taken to reach that goal. 'To that end' links a goal to the step taken toward it. 'In other words' fails because founding a group is not a restatement of her wish.

C gives the exact number of islands with Komodo dragons (four) and places it against the park's total of twenty-nine, which emphasizes how few islands they occupy. A and B never give a number, and D only gives the park's total.

Officials closed the area because measurements showed the tower rotating in a worrying way, so the second event is a consequence of the first. 'As a result' shows that cause and effect. 'For example' fails because the closure is not an example of the rotation.

The text lists a second requirement of the same amendment (the January 3 swearing-in) after the first (the January 20 inauguration). 'In addition' adds that further point. 'Specifically' fails because the second rule is not a more detailed version of the first.

To explain where the name came from, the sentence must connect 'Mansourasaurus' to the Mansoura University team, and only D does that. C names the discoverers but never says the species was named after them.

D opens the story chronologically with the series' 2012 premiere and signals that it would later be nominated for an award, so it begins a narrative about the award-nominated series. A starts the story but leaves out the nomination, and B and C summarize the outcome rather than beginning a narrative (C never even names the series).

A summary should state what was studied and the main finding. D does both: it names the study of auk landings and states that success fell as wind intensified. A and B describe the study's setup without its result, and C gives only one isolated statistic.

An advantage is a benefit, and C states one: the format appealed to audiences because it let them control the experience. A, B, and D only describe how the format worked without saying why it was beneficial.

The writer seeks out old libraries across the US, yet even visiting every state would not lead to the oldest one in the hemisphere, since it is in Mexico. 'Nevertheless' signals this contrast with what the first sentence might lead us to expect. 'As a result' fails because the writer's interest does not cause the library to be elsewhere.

The text calls the gigantic jets outliers, and the next clause supports that claim by noting that most jets reach only 20 to 50 km. 'Indeed' introduces information that reinforces and strengthens the previous point. 'Nevertheless' wrongly suggests a contrast, and 'consequently' wrongly suggests the typical heights are caused by the outliers.
B identifies what the two feeding methods have in common: neither one requires diving into the water. C points out a difference, and A and D describe the methods without stating a similarity.
Few people know Pollard's name, but many have seen her work, which is a contrast. 'However' signals it. 'Therefore' fails because seeing her work doesn't follow from not knowing her name.
The sentence gives specific instances (giocoso, lento) of the descriptive Italian notations just mentioned, so 'For example' fits. 'On the other hand' wrongly signals a contrast.
The text walks through the steps of a dig in order (begins, then, ...), and removing and analyzing the artifacts is the last step. 'Finally' marks that last step. 'Earlier' gets the order backward.

The text presents two different ways to deal with contaminated soil: hauling it to a landfill or detoxifying it with plants. 'Alternatively' introduces the second option. 'For example' fails because phytoremediation is not an example of moving soil to a landfill.

B states what the two cities share: in both, thousands gather for water fights to celebrate Songkran. A emphasizes a difference, C mentions a difference without naming the similarity, and D doesn't mention either city.

C directly states that the novel retells the epic from the character Kaikeyi's point of view. B mentions how Patel portrays Kaikeyi but not whose point of view the story uses, and A and D are about the original poem.

Saying that sensory experience of the material world is the ultimate source of knowledge is a restatement of Aristotle's view that knowledge comes from engaging directly with that world. 'In other words' introduces a restatement. 'Meanwhile' wrongly suggests a separate, simultaneous point.

The volcanoes look alike from afar, but volcanologists can tell they are different types, which is a contrast. 'Though' signals it. 'Therefore' fails because experts' ability to tell them apart doesn't follow from their similar appearance.

The first sentence says what Duchamp intended, and the second confirms that the work did exactly that. 'Indeed' introduces information that confirms and reinforces a previous statement. 'Instead' wrongly suggests the sculpture did something other than what was intended.
Lowering the voting age caused many more people to gain the chance to vote, so 'As a result' shows the cause-and-effect link. 'Nevertheless' wrongly signals a contrast.

The text describes 'opposing effects' and begins with 'On one hand' for the effect that strengthens the storm. 'On the other hand' completes the pair by introducing the effect that weakens it. 'In other words' fails because the second effect is not a restatement of the first.

Only D gives both numbers (about 1,200 falls versus over 60,000 finds) and uses 'while' to set them against each other. A and B define the categories without numbers, and C gives only the number of falls.

The bags were impractical, yet they still dominated the market because they were the only ones that could be mass-produced. 'However' signals this contrast with what we'd expect. 'Thus' wrongly suggests their impracticality caused their dominance.

An audience unfamiliar with historical analysis needs it identified and defined, and C does both: it calls it an approach to art criticism and says it considers the historical context of a work. A and B focus on texture analysis, and D gives an example without explaining the concept.

A stresses the harshness by calling tundra winters especially harsh and giving the frigid -30 degrees Fahrenheit average. C highlights the mild growing season and plant variety, which works against the goal, and B and D focus on what can survive there.

The first sentence says many authors have created hybrid works of poetry and prose, and Evaristo's verse novel is one such work. 'For example' introduces it as an instance. 'By contrast' fails because the book fits the general claim instead of opposing it.

Research methods describe what the researchers actually did: D says they collected rock samples from two seafloor ridges and analyzed their age and oxidation levels. A and C focus on the study's goals, and B mixes a purpose with background about the Archean eon.
The text announces three questions and then lists them with 'Second' and 'Finally', so the first question should be introduced with 'First'. 'Additionally' doesn't work for the first item in a list.

For readers who don't know Park, D introduces her (a Korean American artist) and describes what the work does: light passes through a tile-fitted fence and forms colorful prisms. A refers to 'Park' without introducing her, B doesn't describe the work, and C skips both the introduction and the effect of light.

Because each compound reflects a unique light pattern, De Sanctis could identify sodium carbonate by analyzing the light from Ceres. The second sentence is a consequence of the first, so 'Thus' fits. 'Regardless' wrongly suggests her finding happened in spite of the first fact.

Since the audience already knows Mukherjee, the sentence should focus on the novel itself, and C names the novel and describes its two central characters. A never names the novel, while B and D spend their space introducing the author instead of describing the book.

A compares the two hypotheses directly: Fodor's treats only some cognitive systems as modular, so it is less expansive than Carruthers's MMH, which includes all of them. C is inaccurate because both hypotheses treat low-level systems as modular, and B and D describe Carruthers's proposal without clearly comparing the scope of the two.
D gives Sirius A's mass (2.063 solar masses) and puts it in context by noting it is more massive than the Sun. None of the other choices even mentions Sirius A.

A emphasizes significance by showing what the discovery led to: deciphering the genetic code and better understanding how genetic variations affect health. D mentions the discovery's importance but shifts the focus to Ochoa's mistaken hypothesis, and B and C just describe the enzyme.

B gives both tunnels' lengths and notes that the Channel Tunnel is slightly shorter, which is a direct comparison. A and C mention only one tunnel's length, and D compares only what type of tunnel each is.

D directly contrasts the two kinds of breeds: those with erect, wolf-like ears can make the 'ears rotator' action, while those with flopped or semi-flopped ears cannot. B reverses the finding, A contradicts the notes, and C compares the ears themselves rather than the breeds.

To refute the claim, the sentence must show that malapportionment favors rural districts, not small urban ones. D does this, explaining that the formula's extra points for land overrepresent less populated rural districts. A supports the claim instead, and B wrongly says more populated districts are overrepresented.

D presents both the study (Chinsamy-Turan's 2021 analysis of Sahara pterosaur jawbones) and its findings (few growth lines, so the bones were juveniles'). A stops at her initial uncertainty, and B and C describe the study without its conclusion.

If varied behavior requires bigger, costlier brains, it logically follows that animals with only basic behaviors should invest less in brain tissue. 'Thus' introduces that conclusion. 'Nevertheless' wrongly signals a contrast, and 'Subsequently' signals a time sequence that isn't there.
D names Brook Farm and uses Ripley's own words to state its goal. A uses the quotation but never mentions Brook Farm, and B and C don't quote Ripley at all.

The notes show 327 of 357 nearby stars are cooler than the Sun and only 11 are hotter, so A's claim that the Sun is hotter than most but not all nearby stars captures its relative temperature. C gives data about cooler stars but never mentions the Sun's temperature, and D only says how the Sun is classified.

B states what the two sculptures share: both show African American figures in poses that symbolize supportive relationships. A describes only one sculpture, C gives two different dates, and D emphasizes a difference.

Topographic maps show land above sea level, while bathymetric maps show land below the sea, so the two are being contrasted. 'By contrast' signals that. 'For example' fails because bathymetric maps are not an example of topographic maps.
C points out a shared feature, that both paintings are huge, and backs it up with their dimensions. A, B, and D all emphasize differences between the paintings or their artists.

C emphasizes relative size by explicitly saying Hanoi is larger than Ulaanbaatar, while also noting that Ulaanbaatar holds a bigger share of its country's population. A and D just list the numbers without comparing them, and B is confusingly worded and never directly compares the two cities.

A definition explains what a term means, and D does exactly that: georeferencing is assigning geographic coordinates to an image so mapping software can place it in its real location. A, B, and C mention georeferencing in the context of a project without defining it clearly.

The first sentence says broadly that Sauer challenged prevailing views; the second explains exactly what his challenge was. 'Specifically' introduces that more detailed explanation. 'Therefore' fails because his argument is not a result of his challenge but the challenge itself.

For an unfamiliar audience, D names the act, says what it did (abolished the national-origins quota system), and explains why that mattered by noting the system favored northern Europeans. C says what the act did but not why it was significant, and A and B describe the old system without explaining the act's effect.

B mentions both orders, Hymenoptera and Coleoptera, and identifies which animals belong to each, which emphasizes how invertebrates are classified into different orders. A and D mention only one order, and C focuses on threats from invasive species.
C describes the wok's physical shape: a round, wide base and high, angled sides. D mentions the wok's design but only in terms of what it does, and A and B focus on Grace Young's book.

A quotes Acquah's reason for using pointillism (to create an 'illusion of movement') and connects it to the dancing, twirling women in 'Exquisite.' C quotes her description of the technique but not its purpose, and D's quotation is about her subjects, not her technique.

Because the Human Genome Project showed that genes are shaped by interactions with other genes' proteins, researchers have expanded their focus to the proteome. 'Accordingly' signals an action taken in response to that lesson. 'In other words' fails because the second sentence is a consequence, not a restatement.

C highlights differences between the portraits: one is a 2003 painting and the other a 2016 drawing. A and B stress what the portraits have in common, and D compares the subjects rather than the portraits.

The Spartans' one-word reply to Philip II is an example of their concise wit under threat. 'For instance' introduces that example. 'In other words' fails because the anecdote illustrates the claim rather than restating it.

C uses a quotation that points to a problem: claims about the networks are 'disconnected from evidence.' B quotes the same study but only the part about CMNs' popularity, A quotes Simard in support of the theory, and D has no quotation.

C contrasts the fine wool of Merino and Rambouillet sheep (used for apparel) with the thicker Romney wool (used for rugs and blankets). A and B say Romney wool is different without saying how, and D doesn't mention any breed.
D states what the two books share: both describe surreal events in otherwise ordinary places. A and C emphasize differences, and B just gives two different publication dates.

The study's conclusion was that Tibetan mastiffs got their high-altitude mutations by interbreeding with Tibetan wolves about 24,000 years ago, which is what D states. B presents the evidence the researchers noticed (shared mutations) but not the conclusion they drew from it, and A and C leave the study out entirely.

C covers both requirements: duration ('Since 2003') and purpose (preserving Gullah culture through their museums). B gives the purpose but no time span for their work, and A and D don't focus on the two women at all.

The text says the dream of US maglev trains is unrealized, and the next sentence strengthens that point: every operating maglev train is in Asia. 'In fact' introduces information that reinforces and intensifies the previous claim. 'Nevertheless' and 'That said' wrongly signal a contrast.

D states a specific difference: surface-dwelling tetras can see and cave-dwelling tetras cannot. A says they are different without saying how, B describes only cave dwellers, and C just names the two populations.

The poem follows a traditional form, yet Al-Malaika still broke new ground in its subject matter, so the sentence presents a contrast with the traditional form just described. 'Though' signals that contrast. 'In fact' and 'moreover' would suggest the innovation simply adds to or reinforces the poem's traditionalism.

Theory says a ring outside the Roche limit should clump into a moon, but Morgado's team found an intact ring well outside Quaoar's Roche limit. That finding goes against the expectation, so 'though' fits. 'For example' and 'fittingly' wrongly suggest the finding matches the theory.

The poems usually follow sonnet rules like the fourteen-line length, but this twelve-line poem breaks them. 'By contrast' signals that departure. 'For example' fails because the poem is an exception to the pattern, not an example of it.

The text says the differences between the editions are extreme, and the next clause emphasizes just how extreme: some critics treat the two editions as different novels. 'In fact' introduces this stronger supporting point. 'Nevertheless' and 'by contrast' wrongly suggest a contrast, and 'in other words' fails because the critics' view goes beyond simply restating the claim.
A makes the order clear: Alaska was the 49th state and joined several months before Hawaii, the 50th. C says only that they joined the same year, and B and D focus on the new flag.

The text first stresses that iconicity was linked to learning signs, then concedes a limit to that point: frequency was even more strongly linked. 'Granted' introduces a concession that qualifies a previous claim. 'In fact' and 'As a result' would wrongly treat the weaker correlation as support for or a consequence of the first finding.

C presents the study's findings (gas giants with thermal inversions tended to contain heat-absorbing metals) plus the likely explanation, using the term 'thermal inversion' without defining it, which suits an audience that already knows it. D gives the same finding but wastes space defining the term, and A and B don't state the main finding.

Moss and Marlow wanted good roles for their female friends, and they created Six, with six starring queens, to achieve that goal. 'To that end' links the goal to the action taken to reach it. 'For example' fails because the show isn't an example of their goal.

The readings are sent to the BIPM in France, and the next sentence describes the work done at that place. 'There' refers back to that location. 'In particular' and 'For example' fail because the metrologists' work isn't a detail or instance of the readings being sent.

B explains an advantage: because microprobes are tiny, they could explore areas the heavy, wheeled rovers can't reach. A is about rovers, C only says microprobes have been proposed, and D notes a similarity instead of an advantage.

Methodology is how the study was carried out, and B describes that: Kind's team examined the student policies of 132 medical schools to answer their question. C gives the results, D gives only the goal, and A misrepresents the study.

B explains why nautical miles are used: they match the latitude coordinates on nautical charts, which account for Earth's curvature, so distances at sea can be calculated efficiently. A describes the link to latitude without giving a reason, C contradicts the notes about latitude and longitude, and D is about charts, not nautical miles.
A generalization makes a broad statement about ultramarathons as a group, and C does this by saying they range from a few dozen to a few hundred miles. A, B, and D talk only about specific races.

An overview of the chain should show what it connects, and C identifies both ends: pickers in Oregon and wealthy buyers in Japan. A focuses on the chain's origins, B defines commodity chains in general, and D describes only one end.
D specifies where Ctesiphon was: near present-day Baghdad, Iraq. B names Ctesiphon but gives no location, and A and C don't mention the city.

C summarizes the hypothesis's main idea: humans may have reached the Americas by sea, moving along Pacific islands and coastlines while living off a variety of resources. B names the hypothesis without explaining it, and A and D give only supporting details.
